published_source: Printed Table 5, column (7) of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.4968.pdf, p. 7137), read Nov 4 2026: 1.004 in exponentiated form with t = [-0.06], N 91,946; recorded as ln(1.004) = 0.004 with no SE. The printed value has the wrong sign for its own t-statistic; the authors' code gives b = -0.0020584 (exp(b) = 0.998), t = -0.06, N 91,946, in authors_code_*. Earlier: Authors' Stata log logs/2_stata_regressions.smcl and esttab output tables/TABLE_05_hacks_xtlogit.tex in the package; no article text or PDF in the project, so the values are checked against the authors' code output only, not against the printed article.
replication_status: failed (sign: printed Table 5 column (7) 1.004 [t -0.06], i.e. ln 0.004, vs authors' code -0.0020584 (0.0356942), N 91,946 both; the printed coefficient contradicts its own t-statistic and the code reproduces the t-statistic, so the printed value is a probable typographical error; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: Table 5 column 7 (Log breach size): xtreg log_breach_size sinceAPI_0_2yr_post i.date if year < 2016, fe cluster(gvkey) (replication_package_MS-INS-22-01020/programs/2_stata_regressions.do line 1080). Outcome log_breach_size = log records exposed in PRC breach events (hacks.dta), set to 0 for firm-quarters without a breach (line 247). Treatment sinceAPI_0_2yr_post = 1 if 0 <= sinceAPIq <= 8 (lines 220-221): a 0-2-years-post WINDOW indicator that switches off nine quarters after adoption. The table is printed with eform: 0.998 = exp(b) with t = -0.06. Authors' log: b = -0.0020584, SE = 0.0356942, N = 91,946 (incl. 11 merge duplicates), 4,320 firms; fixest on the authors' row-level sample reproduces all four exactly. ELIGIBILITY DECISION (PROTOCOL 5b): kept. The regression is linear with firm and quarter FE, a single binary regressor switching on at firm-specific adoption quarters, and no controls; the window indicator is a treatment that switches off by construction, so the switch-off rule (Hull fn 6) applies. DEVIATION: post-adoption rows with sinceAPIq > 8 are dropped through sample_filter (1,213 of 2,000 post-adoption rows before 2016; 25 adopters whose every pre-2016 row is more than eight quarters after adoption lose all rows), because the gvar path does not apply run_spec's treat_var switch-off drop and treat_var would misclassify long-ago adopters (indicator 0 throughout) as never-treated. After the drop D = 1[date >= api_treat_date_q] equals the authors' indicator in every remaining row. TWFE on the protocol sample: b = 0.0406321, SE = 0.0415338, N = 90,724 firm-quarters (sum of weights 90,733), 4,295 firms, outcome SD 0.284207, expected standardized TWFE 0.142967; the published -0.0021 is therefore NOT the comparison target for run_spec (the authors' estimate uses the 9+ quarter rows as controls). Protocol sample: 123 adopters, 108 adopting by 2015Q4 (86 switchers in 31 cohorts, 20 always-treated), 15 adopting in 2016-2019 are not-yet-treated through 2015 and enter as never-treated (as in the authors' coding). The outcome is very sparse: 82 firm-quarters with a breach, 7 of them treated. Data: shipped analysis_dataset/api_compustat_gvkey_quarterly_sictreated.dta (Compustat x ProgrammableWeb firm-quarters, original data), rebuilt in R following 2_stata_regressions.do lines 121-262: drop if ln_mkt_val missing or sic_code empty (133,292 firm-quarters, 4,748 firms, 2007Q1-2020Q3 = Stata %tq 188-242, 55 quarters); date = quarterly(year, quarter); api_treat_date_q = qofd(api_treat_date); sinceAPIq = date - api_treat_date_q; dmerge gvkey dateq using hacks.dta (1:m, _merge == 2 dropped) adds 11 duplicate firm-quarters (11 firm-quarters each matched to two PRC breach events; 133,303 rows). Prepared file ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2023.4968/api_panel_collapsed.rds collapses the 11 merge duplicates to one row per firm-quarter (outcome = mean of the duplicated rows; all other columns identical within the duplicates) with frequency weight w_mergedup = number of authors' rows (2 for 11 firm-quarters, 1 otherwise). This reproduces the authors' row-level OLS exactly (identical normal equations and cluster scores) while giving the runner a proper firm-quarter panel: with the duplicates kept, estimators.R's anyDuplicated(id, t) > 0 test would switch CSA to the repeated-cross-section att_gt(panel = FALSE) path for a firm panel. The authors' row-level sample is kept in api_panel_authors_sample.rds. Treatment: gvar = api_treat_date_q (quarter of first public API); api_treat_post equals 1[date >= api_treat_date_q] in every row (verified), 0 for the 4,569 never-adopters, absorbing (no switch-offs). Full sample: 179 adopters with 50 distinct adoption quarters (2005-2019); 100 switchers in 41 cohorts observed before and after adoption; 74 adopters treated at their first observed quarter (always-treated; 16 adopted before 2007Q1 and are dated at 2007Q1 by run_spec's gvar mapping); 5 adopt after their last observation. Never-treated firms: 96.2% of firms, 95.0% of rows. Unbalanced panel (entry/exit), so run_spec uses the composition-fixed CSA cells. Cluster gvkey as published. reghdfe drops 101 singletons (published N); run_spec keeps them (same point estimate).
article_check_nov2: Article Table 5 column 7 prints 1.004 (exponentiated) with t = [-0.06], N 91,946. The package log gives b = -0.0020584 (exp(b) = 0.998, t = -0.06). The printed 1.004 has the wrong sign for its own t-statistic, so published_coef keeps the log value; flagged for the lead. Static spec: no event_structure; pre-2007 adopters are always treated in this window either way, so the true-date change does not affect it.
